17 The motor of a crane lifts a load of mass 600 kg. The load rises vertically at a constant speed of
12 m per minute.
What is the useful power output of the motor?
A
0.12 kW
B
1.2 kW
C
7.2 kW
D
71 kW

hints: Notice the load moves at constant speed, so the lifting force equals the weight $mg$ of the $600 \text{ kg}$ load, and the speed $12 \text{ m per minute}$ must be changed to $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Recall useful power for steady lifting is $P = Fv = mgv$, with $g$ about $9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ giving $P$ in $\text{W}$.
First calculate $v = 12/60 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, then multiply by $600 \times 9.81$ and convert the result in $\text{W}$ to $\text{kW}$ to compare with the options.
walkthrough: Constant vertical speed means resultant force is zero, so motor force $F$ equals weight $W = mg = 600 \times 9.81 \text{ N}$.
Convert the speed to SI units: $v = 12 \text{ m per minute} = 12/60 \text{ m s}^{-1} = 0.20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Useful power for a force moving its point of application is $P = Fv = mgv$.
Convert to kilowatts: $1180 \text{ W} \approx 1.18 \text{ kW}$, about $1.2 \text{ kW}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: Gives $0.12 \text{ kW}$, about 10 times too small, from an extra factor of 10 error in converting $12 \text{ m per minute}$ to $\text{m s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: Gives about $1200 \text{ W} = 1.2 \text{ kW}$ from $P = mgv$ with $v = 0.20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: Gives $7.2 \text{ kW}$, which is $600 \times 10 \times 1.2$, using $1.2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ instead of $12/60 = 0.20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: Gives about $71 \text{ kW}$, which is $mg \times 12$, using $12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and forgetting to divide by 60 s to convert per minute to per second.
